_comment: Fixed monitor-mode panel, TD-100/ADR-0013 steps 1-4 build, populated across two sessions (2026-08-30, the second recovering from a power-interrupted first). Each entry pins one measurement (report_id, and input for multi-input tests) together with CLIO's verdict and OONI's real answer AT THE TIME IT WAS ADDED to the panel, so a later monitor run can tell apart a CLIO-side regression (clio_verdict changed since the entry was recorded) from external drift (ooni's own answer changed) on the exact same measurement, rather than lumping both under one alarm. Both CLIO's clio_verdict and OONI's booleans were re-verified live/fresh at seeding time, not copied from older audit rows -- see reports.md for why that mattered (a stale FAILED-verdict signal population turned out to have been superseded by TD-102's later discard fix). dnscheck is deliberately excluded (DEGENERATE-EXEMPT, TD-103: OONI's own anomaly/confirmed/failure fields show zero variance for dnscheck). psiphon's population is OK-only by construction, not by sampling shortfall: every non-OK (FAILED) psiphon candidate sampled disagreed with OONI's own ANOMALOUS answer (93/103, ~90%) -- a real, separate, unresolved finding reported in reports.md, not a panel-seeding gap. signal/whatsapp/telegram have no live FAILED or CONFIRMED verdicts in Kenya's current data (confirmed via a live GROUP BY before seeding) -- OK/ANOMALOUS is the full available diversity today. TD-68 (uptime.signal.org canary -- the relay prompt that requested this work called it 'TD-71', which is actually a different, unrelated TLS-evidence-tiering item; see reports.md for the correction) IS seeded below: it lives under test_name=signal, not dnscheck, so DEGENERATE-EXEMPT does not apply to it -- one live, still-canary-tagged, post-fix measurement (OK/OK agreement) is pinned as entry #144, seeded as the BEST AVAILABLE fixture, not a working regression lock: check_panel() compares a panel row's stored clio_verdict against itself (never re-queries BigQuery for a fresh verdict, confirmed by tracing what would happen if this exact measurement regressed), so this entry today only monitors OONI-side drift on this measurement, not the CLIO-side misclassification TD-68 actually was. TD-93 (whispersystems/signal_legacy_nxdomain) is NOT seeded, for a stronger reason than check_panel()'s limitation: the 5,792 live measurements still carrying signal_legacy_endpoint_nxdomain_only=TRUE all resolve to ooni_verdict IS NULL in int.ooni_measurement_verdicts (CLIO deliberately excludes them from classification post-TD-102-fix) -- there is nothing live to pin at all, not even in this limited form. See reports.md for the full evidence and the recommendation both be revisited if the harness's regression-check logic is ever extended to re-query CLIO's live verdict. SCHEMA v2 (TD-124): three new fields added to every entry -- clio_verdict_now, clio_verdict_refreshed_at, clio_verdict_source (all null until the first `--mode refresh-panel` run populates them). `clio_verdict` above is the permanent seed lock and must never be overwritten by a refresh -- it is the fixed known-answer this panel exists to protect. `clio_verdict_now` is a periodically-refreshed snapshot of CLIO's live verdict for the same measurement_id, written only by `--mode refresh-panel` (a narrow, measurement_id-scoped BigQuery query against int.ooni_measurement_verdicts, never joined to raw_test_keys). check_panel() compares clio_verdict against clio_verdict_now to detect a real CLIO-side regression, gated on clio_verdict_source.verdict_table_modified not being older than the table's current `modified` metadata (a staleness check, since refresh is a deliberate, human-triggered snapshot, not a live query on every monitor run -- TD-124, see reports.md). A legitimate, deliberate change to what 'correct' means for an entry must be made by editing clio_verdict itself with a TD reference in the commit message -- never by letting a routine refresh silently redefine the lock.
